question: Should phase one permit native archive when fresh process-local status and OpenClaw binding checks pass, but cross-process safety still depends on explicit operator confirmation that no other Codex runner owns the thread?
rationale: Codex does not expose a cross-process lease or ownership signal at the inspected revision, so code and tests cannot eliminate the documented concurrent-client risk.

options.title: Accept confirmation-gated archive
options.body: Ship local archive with the current fresh-status, descendant, binding, and explicit confirmation guards while keeping paired-node archive unavailable.

options.title: Defer archive controls
options.body: Ship session listing and safe local branching, but wait for a Codex cross-process lease or equivalent ownership signal before exposing archive.

recommendation.title: Accept confirmation-gated archive
recommendation.body: Ship local archive with the current fresh-status, descendant, binding, and explicit confirmation guards while keeping paired-node archive unavailable.
